verdicts.problem: Grade-mapping tension, not a data error: the row maps 4<=s<=18 to neurotox_grade 2, but the schema rubric's grade 1 explicitly covers 'transient acute behavioural signs resolving within hours-days', and Hagedorn states signs waned 2-4 h post-dose and 'almost never' reappeared from 24 h to 7 days with no euthanasia below a score of 20. Grade 2 is arguable via the rubric's 'clinically significant but manageable/resolving neurologic adverse event' clause, but it should say so; as written the same acute reversible phenomenon is graded 1, 2 or 3 in different lanes of this dataset by different ad-hoc mappings.

correction.notes_add: Grade 2 justified under the rubric's 'clinically significant but resolving neurologic AE' clause; signs resolved 2-4 h with no neuronal loss.

verdicts.problem: Grade-mapping tension, not a data error: the row maps 4<=s<=18 to neurotox_grade 2, but the schema rubric's grade 1 explicitly covers 'transient acute behavioural signs resolving within hours-days', and Hagedorn states signs waned 2-4 h post-dose and 'almost never' reappeared from 24 h to 7 days with no euthanasia below a score of 20. Grade 2 is arguable via the rubric's 'clinically significant but manageable/resolving neurologic adverse event' clause, but it should say so; as written the same acute reversible phenomenon is graded 1, 2 or 3 in different lanes of this dataset by different ad-hoc mappings.

correction.notes_add: Grade 2 justified under the rubric's 'clinically significant but resolving neurologic AE' clause; signs resolved 2-4 h with no neuronal loss.

No siRNA B animal reached score 6 (tremors/seizure) or 7 (death) - the maximum plotted score is 5 - and the group is not statistically separable from PBS (P=0.0845, n=4). The grade rests on the row's own note that 'siRNAs produce more severe acute activation than ASOs, including prolonged and fatal seizures', but that sentence in the paper is about siRNA A's dose response, not siRNA B; what the paper says about siRNA B is only that severity was 'comparable between sequences within the same oligonucleotide class'. summary: 50/50 rows checked against the primary source; every source was retrievable, so there are no UNVERIFIABLE rows. Verdicts: 25 CONFIRMED, 18 CONFIRMED_MINOR, 7 REFUTED (4 major, 3 minor). The batch label is largely wrong: 30 of the 50 rows are not figure-derived at all - 22 are exact reads of a supplementary spreadsheet column (Hagedorn 2022 Suppl_TableS1.xlsx, all 22 matched to the digit against the file) and 8 are exact reads of printed patent tables in US11851654B2 (Tables 2/6/10/14, all 8 matched exactly, including the correct 6 umol dose for Example 5). Only 19 rows are genuinely figure-derived. Of the 11 figure-derived rows carrying a NUMBER, I could measure 9 against the published image; four of those numbers are wrong (O'Rourke Fig 3B rat 700 ug 3.0 -> 3.33; Fig 5E ASO2 700 ug 4.1 -> 4.25; Fig 5E ASO8_PO 100 ug 4.0 -> 3.75; Bravo-Hernandez Fig 1F ASO J 3.0 -> 3.5). One of those errors (ASO8_PO) crosses the row's own grade threshold and drops it from 3 to 2. The other three major findings are not digitisation errors at all: two patent rows (CMS0372, CMS0444) grade the ASO group 1-2 and call it 'reversible' while the same Example's mortality table in the same patent records 2/6 mice dead within one day, and one Bravo-Hernandez row (CMS1992) grades siRNA B as 3 on the strength of a sentence the paper wrote about siRNA A, when the cited panel shows a maximum individual score of 5 (no seizures, no deaths) and P=0.0845 vs PBS. Disclosure test: PASSED. Every figure-derived numeric row in this batch discloses the digitisation in notes, usually with an explicit error bound. No provenance failure of that kind exists here. The one provenance mismatch runs the other way (CMS2093 cites Fig 5E for a number that is in the Results text, and the figure reports a different statistic).
systematic_issues:
1) ID DRIFT - fix this before applying any correction. All 50 measurement_ids in batch_digitised.json point at DIFFERENT rows in the shipped data/cns_measurements.csv. Matching on (source_id, source_table, oligo_name, dose, duration, value) gives a clean 1:1 remap with a drifting offset of 0 to +7: CMS0372->CMS0372, CMS0424->CMS0420, CMS0444->CMS0440, CMS0453->CMS0449, CMS0481->CMS0476, CMS0489->CMS0484, CMS1329->CMS1314, CMS1652->CMS1645, CMS1680->CMS1673, CMS1688->CMS1681, CMS1699->CMS1692 ... CMS1889->CMS1882, CMS1907->CMS1900, CMS1949->CMS1942, CMS1965->CMS1958, CMS1973->CMS1966, CMS1992->CMS1985, CMS2001->CMS1994, CMS2054->CMS2047, CMS2093->CMS2086 (every batch id after CMS0388 is offset). Applying these verdicts by batch id would corrupt 47 of 50 rows. The batch snapshot is also stale on redistribution: it shows summary_stat for 26 rows that the CSV has already upgraded to cc_by. Whatever exports these batches needs to key off the canonical CSV.

2) THE REAL DIGITISATION FAILURE MODE IS EYEBALLING BAR HEIGHTS INSTEAD OF COUNTING DOTS. Every acute-behaviour figure in this batch plots individual animals as dots on an ORDINAL INTEGER scale with n=3-4 per group. That means the group mean can only be a multiple of 1/n and is recoverable EXACTLY by counting the dots - no digitisation error is necessary. All four wrong values are values that are impossible or unnecessary: 4.1 cannot be a mean of four integers; 3.0, 4.0 and 3.0 were estimates where 3.33, 3.75 and 3.5 were sitting on the page. The rows even declare a +/-0.5 tolerance that is looser than the data actually permit. Rule for the lane: for scatter-and-bar panels with visible per-animal points, read the POINTS and compute the mean; only fall back to bar height when points are not plotted.

3) EXTRACTION STOPPED AT THE FIRST TABLE/PANEL AND MISSED THE ADJACENT SAFETY DATA. The two patent ASO rows read Table 2 / Table 10 ('acute tolerability score') and ignored Table 4 / Table 12 two tables later in the same Example, which record ASO mortality of 2/6 and 2/6 within one day (Example 2: 1/5; Example 5: 1/4). The rubric puts death at grade 3, so both rows are under-graded and their reversibility fields are wrong. Any other row in this dataset sourced from US11851654B2 Examples 1-5 needs the same check. The same pattern shows up in the statistics fields: CMS1957 asserts 'only the 3 mg group reached significance' when Supp Table S3 shows 0.3 mg and 1 mg also significant at 0-15 min and this very group significant at 30-60 min.

4) GRADE MAPPINGS ARE PER-LANE AND MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT. The same phenomenon - acute, dose-dependent, fully reversible behavioural toxicity after central dosing - is graded by four different ad-hoc mappings: Hagedorn (0-20 scale) maps 4-18 to grade 2; O'Rourke IT (0-7) maps s>=3 straight to grade 3 with no grade 2 at all; O'Rourke ICV (0-7) maps 2-4 to 2 and >=4 to 3; Bravo-Hernandez (0-7) maps 3-5 to 2 and >=5 to 3; Moazami (0-75) declares no mapping and grades 18 as 1 and 25 as 2. Consequence: an ASO scoring 3/7 in O'Rourke's IT lane is a grade 3 while a mouse convulsing across all five Hagedorn categories at 13.67/20 is a grade 2. Publish the per-scale band edges as a table in METHODOLOGY.md and reconcile them against the rubric, whose grade 1 explicitly covers 'transient acute behavioural signs resolving within hours-days'.

5) DOSE-GROUP SELECTION SKEWS TOWARD THE NULL DOSE. Five of the nine O'Rourke rows in this batch record the LOWEST dose of a dose-response panel, where every value is 0 - so within this sample the mixed PS/PO series looks uniformly safe, while the same panels show those same PO compounds at 2.0-4.25 at 300-700 ug. The full CSV does carry the other dose groups, so this is a sampling artefact of the batch rather than a dataset defect, but any downstream filter that selects one row per oligo will reproduce the bias.

6) BOILERPLATE NOTES CARRY THE FIRST EXAMPLE'S PARAMETERS ACROSS ALL EXAMPLES. All eight patent rows say 'n=4-7' regardless of which Example they came from (Example 1 n=4-7, Examples 2 and 4 n=4-5, Example 5 n=4 / table footnote n=3-4). The template note was written once and pasted. Same class of error as the dose: CMS0424 got the 6 umol dose right in the field but its note still repeats the Example 1 n.

7) WHAT IS WORKING - keep it. Every genuinely figure-derived numeric row discloses the digitisation and most declare an error bound; the TBD-valued rows (CMS1329, CMS1881, CMS1957, CMS1992, CMS2001, CMS2054, CMS1652) all keep effect_direction and a prose effect_vs_control, which is exactly the honest record the schema asks for. CMS2054 is the reference implementation. The one thing to fix in that group is CMS1652, whose TBD is justified by a claim that the figure is unreadable when it is not.
